senses.simple: The -ing form of "have".
senses.ko: have의 -ing 형태, 가지고 있는, 먹고 있는

examples.en: We are having spaghetti tonight.
examples.ko: 우리는 오늘 밤 스파게티를 먹을 거야.

examples.en: Are you having fun?

senses.simple: Used to talk about the future.
senses.ko_simple: 앞으로 일어날 일을 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: I will call you tomorrow.
It will be sunny this weekend.

senses.simple: Used to ask someone to do something, or to say you agree to do it.
senses.ko_simple: 무언가를 부탁하거나, 하겠다고 약속할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Will you help me carry this?
Okay, I will clean my room now.

senses.simple: The strong wish to do something.

examples.en: She has the will to win.
Where there's a will, there's a way.

senses.simple: Used to talk about something that might happen, or that you imagine.
senses.ko_simple: 어떤 일이 일어난다고 상상하거나 가정할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: If I had wings, I would fly to the moon.
examples.ko: 내가 날개가 있다면 달까지 날아갈 텐데.

examples.en: It would be fun to have a pet dragon.

senses.simple: Used to ask or offer something politely.
senses.ko_simple: 공손하게 묻거나 부탁할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Would you like some lemonade?
Would you please pass the salt?

senses.simple: Used to talk about something that happened many times in the past.
senses.ko_simple: 옛날에 자주 하던 일을 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: When I was little, Grandma would read to me every night.
examples.ko: 내가 어렸을 때 할머니가 매일 밤 책을 읽어 주시곤 했다.

examples.en: We would go swimming every summer.

senses.simple: Used to offer or suggest something, as in "Shall we go?"
senses.ko_simple: 무엇을 함께 하자고 하거나 해 줄지 물어볼 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Shall we dance?
Shall I open the window for you?

senses.simple: A formal or old-fashioned word for "will".

examples.en: We shall meet again someday.
You shall go to the ball, Cinderella!
examples.ko: 신데렐라, 너는 무도회에 가게 될 거야!

senses.simple: Used to say what is a good or right thing to do.
senses.ko_simple: 하는 것이 좋거나 옳은 일을 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: You should wear sunscreen at the beach.
We should be nice to everyone.

senses.simple: Used to say what you expect will happen.
senses.ko_simple: 아마 그렇게 될 거라고 예상할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: The bus should be here soon.
This puzzle should be easy for you.

senses.simple: Used to say that someone is able to do something.
senses.ko_simple: 무엇을 할 수 있는 능력이 있다는 뜻

examples.en: I can swim across the pool.
examples.ko: 나는 수영장 끝까지 헤엄칠 수 있다.

examples.en: Can you whistle?

senses.simple: Used to ask for or give permission.
senses.ko_simple: 해도 되는지 묻거나 허락할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Can I have a cookie?
Yes, you can go outside now.

senses.simple: A metal container for food or drinks.

examples.en: Dad opened a can of soup.
Please put the empty cans in the recycling bin.
examples.ko: 빈 캔은 재활용 통에 넣어 주세요.

senses.simple: The past form of "can": was able to.

examples.en: I could read when I was four.
examples.ko: 나는 네 살 때 글을 읽을 수 있었다.

examples.en: We couldn't see the stars because of the clouds.
examples.ko: 구름 때문에 별을 볼 수 없었다.

senses.simple: Used to ask for something politely.
senses.ko_simple: 공손하게 부탁하거나 허락을 구할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Could you help me with this box?
Could I have some more water, please?
examples.ko: 물 좀 더 주실 수 있을까요?

senses.simple: Used to say that something is possible.
senses.ko_simple: 그럴 수도 있다는 가능성을 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It could rain later.
examples.ko: 우산 챙겨. 이따가 비가 올 수도 있어.

examples.en: That noise could be the cat.

senses.simple: Used to say that something might happen or be true.

examples.en: It may snow tonight.
I may be a little late.

senses.simple: Used to ask for or give permission politely.
senses.ko_simple: 공손하게 허락을 구하거나 허락할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: May I go to the restroom, please?
You may begin the test now.

senses.simple: May: the fifth month of the year, after April.
senses.ko_simple: 일 년 중 다섯 번째 달

examples.en: My birthday is in May.
Flowers bloom everywhere in May.

senses.simple: Used to say that something is possible but not sure.
senses.ko_simple: 확실하지 않지만 그럴 수도 있다는 뜻

examples.en: We might go to the zoo on Saturday.
Bring a jacket. It might get cold.

senses.simple: Great strength or power.

examples.en: He pushed the heavy door with all his might.
examples.ko: 그는 있는 힘을 다해 무거운 문을 밀었다.

examples.en: The knight fought with great might.

senses.simple: Used to say that something is very important to do, or is a rule.
senses.ko_simple: 꼭 해야 하는 일이나 규칙을 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.
We must be quiet during the test.

senses.simple: Used to say that you are almost sure something is true.
senses.ko_simple: 거의 확실하다고 생각할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: You must be tired after that long hike.
Someone is at the door. It must be Grandma.
examples.ko: 누가 문 앞에 왔어. 할머니가 틀림없어.

senses.simple: A word you use to make a sentence mean the opposite, or to say no.

examples.en: I am not sleepy yet.
Please do not touch the paintings.

senses.simple: A word you say to answer a question when the answer is not yes.

examples.en: "Do you want broccoli?" "No, thank you."
No, I didn't break the vase!

senses.simple: Not any.

examples.en: There is no milk left.
I have no idea where my shoe went.

senses.simple: Used on signs to say something is not allowed.

examples.en: The sign says "No swimming."
No running in the hallway!

senses.simple: A word you say to agree or to answer a question when the answer is true.

examples.en: "Are you ready?" "Yes, I am!"
Yes, you can have another cookie.
examples.ko: 그래, 쿠키 하나 더 먹어도 돼.

senses.simple: Something you shout when you are very happy about something.

examples.en: Yes! We won the game!
Yes! No school tomorrow!

senses.simple: A friendly, everyday way to say "yes".

examples.en: "Want to play?" "Yeah, sure!"
Yeah, I saw that movie. It was awesome.
examples.ko: 응, 그 영화 봤어. 정말 멋졌어.

senses.simple: A word that means "yes" or "all right".

examples.en: "Can you set the table?" "Okay, Mom!"
Okay, everyone, let's start the game.

senses.simple: All right; not bad, or not hurt.

examples.en: Are you okay? You fell pretty hard.
The food was okay, but not great.

senses.simple: A short way to write "okay": yes, or all right.

examples.en: "Clean up your toys." "OK!"
Is it OK if I sit here?

senses.simple: A polite word you add when you ask for something.
senses.ko_simple: 무언가를 부탁할 때 예의 바르게 붙이는 말

examples.en: Can I have some water, please?
Please close the door.

senses.simple: To make someone happy.

examples.en: I cleaned my room to please my mom.
examples.ko: 엄마를 기쁘게 해 드리려고 방을 치웠다.

examples.en: It's hard to please my picky little brother.

senses.simple: A word you say to greet someone or when you answer the phone.
senses.ko_simple: 사람을 만났을 때나 전화를 받을 때 하는 인사말

examples.en: Hello, Mrs. Kim! How are you?
Hello? Who is this?

senses.simple: A friendly, short way to say hello.

examples.en: Hi, Emma! Want to play?
Say hi to your mom for me.

senses.simple: A word you say when you leave someone or someone leaves you.

examples.en: Goodbye! See you tomorrow!
We waved goodbye to Grandma at the airport.
examples.ko: 우리는 공항에서 할머니께 손을 흔들며 작별 인사를 했다.

senses.simple: A short, friendly way to say goodbye.

examples.en: Bye, Mom! I'm going to school.
Bye! Have a fun weekend!

senses.simple: A short, friendly way to say "thank you".

examples.en: Thanks for helping me with my homework!
"Here's your pencil." "Thanks!"

senses.simple: Words or actions that show you are grateful.

examples.en: We give thanks for our food on Thanksgiving.
examples.ko: 추수감사절에 우리는 음식에 대해 감사를 드린다.

examples.en: Thanks to you, we won the game!

senses.simple: A word you say when you feel surprised, happy, sad, or when you suddenly understand something.
senses.ko_simple: 놀라거나, 기쁘거나, 슬프거나, 무언가를 갑자기 깨달았을 때 하는 말

examples.en: Oh no! I forgot my lunch!
Oh, now I understand.

senses.simple: A word you say when you are very surprised or amazed.
senses.ko_simple: 아주 놀라거나 감탄했을 때 하는 말

examples.en: Wow! Look at that giant pumpkin!
examples.ko: 우와! 저 거대한 호박 좀 봐!

examples.en: Wow, you got a perfect score!

senses.simple: A word you say to get someone's attention, or a friendly way to say hi.
senses.ko_simple: 누군가를 부르거나 친근하게 인사할 때 하는 말

examples.en: Hey, wait for me!
Hey, Sam! How was your weekend?

senses.simple: Feeling bad about something you did wrong.
senses.ko_simple: 내가 잘못한 일에 대해 미안한 마음이 드는

examples.en: I'm sorry I broke your crayon.
Say sorry to your sister.

senses.simple: Feeling sad for someone who has a problem.
senses.ko_simple: 다른 사람의 안 좋은 일에 마음이 아픈

examples.en: I'm sorry your hamster is sick.
We felt sorry for the lost puppy.

senses.simple: Used to ask someone to say something again.
senses.ko_simple: 잘 못 들어서 다시 말해 달라고 할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: Sorry? I didn't hear you.
Sorry, can you say that again?

senses.simple: In or to this place.

examples.en: Come here and look at this bug!
examples.ko: 이리 와서 이 벌레 좀 봐!

examples.en: I have lived here all my life.

senses.simple: Used when you give something to someone, as in "Here you are."

examples.en: Here is your sandwich.
Here you go. Enjoy your ice cream!

senses.simple: In or to that place, not here.

examples.en: Put your coat over there.
We went to Hawaii and swam there every day.
examples.ko: 우리는 하와이에 가서 거기서 매일 수영했다.

senses.simple: Used with "is" or "are" to say that something exists.
senses.ko_simple: 'there is', 'there are'로 무엇이 있다고 말할 때 쓰는 말

examples.en: There is a frog in the pond.
There are 26 letters in the English alphabet.

senses.simple: At this time; at this moment.

examples.en: It's raining now, so let's stay inside.
I'm ready now. Let's go!

senses.simple: Right away; immediately.

examples.en: Come here right now!
We need to leave now or we'll be late.
examples.ko: 지금 바로 출발해야 해, 안 그러면 늦어.

senses.simple: At that time, in the past or future.

examples.en: I was only five then.
Let's meet at noon. See you then!

senses.simple: Next; after that.

examples.en: First brush your teeth, then go to bed.
examples.ko: 먼저 이를 닦고, 그다음에 자러 가.

examples.en: We went to the museum and then had lunch.

senses.simple: In that case; so.

examples.en: If you're hungry, then eat a snack.
"I finished my homework." "Then you can play."

senses.simple: On this day.

examples.en: Today is my birthday!
It is very windy today.

senses.simple: In these times; nowadays.

examples.en: Today, many people use phones to take pictures.
examples.ko: 오늘날 많은 사람들이 휴대폰으로 사진을 찍는다.

examples.en: Many Cherokee people live in Oklahoma today.
examples.ko: 오늘날 많은 체로키족 사람들이 오클라호마에 산다.

senses.simple: On the night of today.

examples.en: We are having tacos for dinner tonight.
Look, there's a full moon tonight.

senses.simple: On the day after today.

examples.en: We have a field trip tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

senses.simple: The future.

examples.en: The kids of today are the leaders of tomorrow.
Who knows what tomorrow will bring?
examples.ko: 앞으로 무슨 일이 일어날지 누가 알겠어?

senses.simple: On the day before today.

examples.en: I lost a tooth yesterday.
It snowed yesterday, so we built a snowman.

senses.simple: One more time.

examples.en: Can we read that story again?
examples.ko: 그 이야기 또 읽어 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: I made a mistake, so I tried again.

senses.simple: Back to the way it was before.

examples.en: I'm glad you're feeling well again.
After the storm, the sun came out again.

senses.simple: Too; as well; in addition.

examples.en: I like dogs, and I also like cats.
She plays piano and also sings.
examples.ko: 그 애는 피아노도 치고 노래도 한다.

senses.simple: Also; as well.

examples.en: I want to come too!
My sister likes pizza, and I do too.

senses.simple: More than is good or needed.

examples.en: This soup is too hot to eat.
examples.ko: 이 수프는 너무 뜨거워서 먹을 수 없다.

examples.en: I ate too much candy, and now my tummy hurts.
examples.ko: 사탕을 너무 많이 먹어서 배가 아프다.

senses.simple: A word that makes another word stronger; really; a lot.
senses.ko_simple: 다른 말의 뜻을 더 강하게 해 주는 말

examples.en: The giraffe is very tall.
Thank you very much!

senses.simple: Only; simply.

examples.en: I just want to sleep for five more minutes.
It's just a little scratch. Don't worry.
examples.ko: 그냥 살짝 긁힌 거야. 걱정 마.

senses.simple: A very short time ago.

examples.en: I just finished my homework.
The bus just left.

senses.simple: Exactly.

examples.en: This hat fits just right.
You look just like your mom.

senses.simple: Nothing more than; just.

examples.en: I only have two dollars.
The store is only open on weekends.

senses.simple: With no others; the one and no more.

examples.en: I am the only kid in my family.
This is the only key to the treasure box.

senses.simple: Used to show that something is surprising.
senses.ko_simple: 놀라운 일을 강조할 때 쓰는 말 ('~조차')

examples.en: My grandpa can even do a cartwheel!
It's so easy that even a baby could do it.
examples.ko: 그건 너무 쉬워서 아기도 할 수 있겠다.

senses.simple: An even number can be split into two equal groups, like 2, 4, 6, and 8.
senses.ko_simple: 2, 4, 6, 8처럼 둘로 똑같이 나눌 수 있는 수의

examples.en: Four is an even number, but five is not.
All the houses on this side have even numbers.

senses.simple: Flat and smooth, or the same.

examples.en: The score is even, five to five.
Make sure the table is even before you put the puzzle on it.
examples.ko: 퍼즐을 올려놓기 전에 탁자가 평평한지 확인해.

senses.simple: Continuing until now; not stopped.

examples.en: Are you still hungry?
It's still raining outside.

senses.simple: Not moving.

examples.en: Please sit still while I braid your hair.
examples.ko: 머리 땋는 동안 가만히 앉아 있어.

examples.en: The lake was very still in the morning.

senses.simple: Even so; but.

examples.en: It was cold. Still, we had fun at the beach.
I lost the race, but I'm still proud of myself.

senses.simple: Before now, or sooner than you expected.

examples.en: I have already eaten lunch.
Is it time for bed already?

senses.simple: Very nearly, but not quite.

examples.en: I'm almost done with my drawing.
I almost fell off my bike!

senses.simple: Almost; not quite.

examples.en: It's nearly time for dinner.
I nearly missed the bus this morning.

senses.simple: Very, or more than a little.

examples.en: The movie was quite long.
It's quite cold today, so wear a coat.

senses.simple: Completely. Often used with "not".

examples.en: I'm not quite ready yet.
You are quite right.

senses.simple: Very; a lot.

examples.en: I really like your new shoes.
examples.ko: 네 새 신발 정말 마음에 든다.

examples.en: The roller coaster was really fast.

senses.simple: In truth; actually. Also said to show surprise.
senses.ko_simple: '진짜로'라는 뜻. 놀랄 때 '정말?' 하고 묻기도 함

examples.en: Did you really see a bear?
"I can wiggle my ears." "Really? Show me!"
examples.ko: "나 귀 움직일 수 있어." "정말? 보여 줘!"

senses.simple: In a short time from now.

examples.en: Dinner will be ready soon.
Get well soon!

senses.simple: At any time. Used in questions and "never"-type sentences.

examples.en: Have you ever seen a shooting star?
This is the best pizza I have ever eaten.
examples.ko: 이건 내가 먹어 본 피자 중 최고다.

senses.simple: Not at any time; not ever.

examples.en: I have never been on an airplane.
examples.ko: 나는 비행기를 한 번도 타 본 적이 없다.

examples.en: Never cross the street without looking both ways.
examples.ko: 양쪽을 보지 않고 길을 건너지 마.

senses.simple: Every time; all the time.

examples.en: I always brush my teeth before bed.
examples.ko: 나는 자기 전에 항상 이를 닦는다.

examples.en: My dog is always happy to see me.
examples.ko: 우리 개는 나를 보면 언제나 반가워한다.

senses.simple: Many times.

examples.en: We often go to the park on Sundays.
How often do you feed your fish?

senses.simple: At some times, but not always.

examples.en: Sometimes I walk to school, and sometimes I take the bus.
examples.ko: 가끔은 걸어서 학교에 가고 가끔은 버스를 탄다.

examples.en: My little brother is sometimes grumpy in the morning.

senses.simple: Most of the time; normally.

examples.en: I usually go to bed at nine o'clock.
It usually snows here in January.

senses.simple: One time.

examples.en: I have been to New York once.
examples.ko: 나는 뉴욕에 한 번 가 봤다.

examples.en: We go to the dentist once a year.
examples.ko: 우리는 일 년에 한 번 치과에 간다.

senses.simple: At some time in the past. "Once upon a time" starts many stories.
senses.ko_simple: 예전 어느 때에. 'once upon a time'은 '옛날 옛적에'

examples.en: Dinosaurs once lived where my town is now.
examples.ko: 한때 우리 마을이 있는 곳에 공룡이 살았다.

examples.en: Once upon a time, there was a little red hen.
examples.ko: 옛날 옛적에 작은 빨간 암탉이 있었다.

senses.simple: As soon as; after.

examples.en: Once you finish your homework, you can play.
Once the sun went down, it got cold.

senses.simple: Two times.

examples.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.ko: 나는 하루에 두 번 이를 닦는다.

examples.en: My dad is twice as tall as my little sister.
examples.ko: 아빠는 여동생보다 키가 두 배 크다.

senses.simple: Perhaps; it is possible.

examples.en: Maybe we can go swimming tomorrow.
examples.ko: 어쩌면 내일 수영하러 갈 수 있을 거야.

examples.en: "Can I have a puppy?" "Maybe someday."

senses.simple: Maybe; possibly. It sounds a little more polite or formal.
senses.ko_simple: 'maybe'와 같은 뜻으로 조금 더 공손한 말

examples.en: Perhaps it will stop raining soon.
Perhaps you left your book at school.
examples.ko: 아마 책을 학교에 두고 왔나 보다.

senses.simple: Other; different; more. Used after words like "someone", "anything", or "what".

examples.en: Do you want anything else to eat?
Everyone else went home early.
examples.ko: 다른 사람들은 모두 일찍 집에 갔다.

senses.simple: "Or else" means "if not, something bad will happen".

examples.en: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
Hold on tight, or else you'll fall.
examples.ko: 꽉 잡아, 안 그러면 떨어질 거야.

senses.simple: In place of something else.

examples.en: We didn't have juice, so I drank milk instead.
Let's walk instead of taking the car.

senses.simple: Can not; is not able to, or is not allowed to. The short form is "can't".
senses.ko_simple: '할 수 없다' 또는 '하면 안 된다'는 뜻 (줄이면 can't)

examples.en: Penguins cannot fly, but they can swim very fast.
examples.ko: 펭귄은 날 수 없지만 아주 빨리 헤엄칠 수 있다.

examples.en: You cannot bring food into the library.
examples.ko: 도서관에 음식을 가지고 들어갈 수 없다.
